source.title: Determinant Estimation under Memory Constraints and Neural Scaling Laws
source.authors: S. Ameli; C. van der Heide; Liam Hodgkinson; Fred Roosta; Michael W. Mahoney

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some equations and tables are affected by PDF text extraction and flattening, but the document is not cut off or the wrong study.
record.tranche_reason: The paper assumes neural scaling laws in test error and uses scaling-law behavior to develop a log-determinant estimation method. Its reported results concern determinants of kernel matrices, not the language-model loss scaling claims.
record.gate_note: The study derives and evaluates scaling behavior for pseudo-determinants and log-determinants of NTK and Matérn kernel matrices. It does not measure held-out language-model pretraining loss, parameter/token/compute scaling of that loss, compute-optimal allocation, architecture effects on that loss, or downstream task performance. Its results below are recorded as related but different measurements under versions ["none"]. Statements about scaling laws from cited prior work are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study assumes power-law test-error scaling for kernel/GP regression (citing prior work) and derives a scaling law for determinant ratios of NTK and Matérn kernel Gram matrices to build a log-determinant extrapolation method (FLODANCE). It reports no held-out pretraining loss of language models, no parameter/token/compute scaling, no compute-optimal allocation, no architecture-shape effects on loss, and no downstream performance. Its scaling is in number of datapoints in a kernel matrix, a different construct from every version, so it tests none.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors present MEMDET, an exact memory-constrained log-determinant algorithm, and, assuming neural scaling laws in test error, derive power-law scaling for kernel determinant ratios. FLODANCE then estimates large NTK log-determinants from small subsets with high accuracy and large speedups, and extends to Matérn-kernel GPs.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce the original language-model loss-scaling measurements. It derives and evaluates determinant-scaling and extrapolation methods for NTK and other kernel matrices.
record.method_sensitivity: FLODANCE accuracy varies with the fitting interval size ns; the paper reports that endpoint prediction error decreases from over 50% to under 0.1% as ns increases. It also reports that data ordering affects the regression output and assesses sensitivity to subsampling.

fits_no_version.finding: Ratios of successive NTK Gram-matrix determinants for trained ResNets on CIFAR-10 follow an approximate power law in n (fitted exponent about -95.3), and FLODANCE fitted on up to 5,000 points extrapolates the 50,000-point log-determinant within 0.2% (ResNet9) and 0.02% (ResNet50) error, stable across subsamples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For trained-network NTK Gram matrices, successive determinant ratios scale as a power of dataset size n, permitting accurate extrapolation of large-n log-determinants from small subsets.

fits_no_version.finding: A multi-output Matérn-kernel GP covariance shows determinant-ratio scaling (~n^-4.22) and FLODANCE extrapolation error below 0.4%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Determinant-ratio power-law scaling and log-determinant extrapolation extend to Matérn-kernel GP covariance matrices.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), as stated in the study metadata
record.problems: The determinant scaling assumption is a premise for the proposed method, not a direct test of language-model loss scaling. Empirical evaluations concern a limited set of trained image models and one Matérn-kernel Gaussian process; the paper itself notes that data ordering affects the fit and that a burn-in can be needed.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-method error entries from Table 2 and runtime entries from Table H.2 are omitted because they compare log-determinant estimation methods rather than measuring any of the listed language-model loss-scaling versions. Results cited from other studies are not included.

untested.parts: Power-law scaling of held-out LM pretraining loss in parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolating LM loss from small to much larger runs (the paper extrapolates kernel log-determinants, not loss).
Effect of depth/width/shape on loss at fixed parameters.
Loss power laws in other modalities or training regimes (image models are used only to form NTKs; their test loss vs scale is not measured).
Downstream task predictability from scale or loss.
Dependence of LM loss exponents or allocation on setup and fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: Rows are correctly linked to none; their 'observed' states refer to the paper's own determinant-scaling assumption, not any version. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only as motivation in the introduction. Table 2 and Table H.2 method comparisons are rightly left out as method-performance results. Sensitivity of extrapolation error to fit-interval size ns (over 50% to under 0.1%, Fig. G.3) concerns the method, not V7.

Prediction of much larger language-model runs' held-out loss from smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation trends.
Effects of language-model depth, width, and architecture on held-out loss at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior of held-out pretraining loss in other modalities or training regimes.
Predictability of downstream-task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of language-model loss exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.stage_stated: trained on a subset of 1000 datapoints from CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Measured ratios of successive empirical NTK Gram-matrix determinants.
rows.note: The paper describes the plotted ratios as exact and shows a best-fit scaling line. This is a determinant-ratio result, not a language-model loss measurement.

rows.subject: ResNet9
rows.operation_detail: Fitted FLODANCE on a subsample and extrapolated the NTK log-determinant to the full dataset size.
rows.measure: Error in extrapolated log-determinant at n = 50,000
rows.note: The paper reports a speedup of (n/ns)^3 = 1000 for this configuration. The result concerns NTK log-determinant extrapolation, not language-model loss.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Fitted FLODANCE on a subsample and extrapolated the NTK log-determinant to the full dataset size.
rows.measure: Error in extrapolated log-determinant at n = 50,000
rows.note: The paper reports a speedup of (n/ns)^3 = 1000 for this configuration. The result concerns NTK log-determinant extrapolation, not language-model loss.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Measured exact NTK log-determinants across 15 independent random subsamples.
rows.measure: Normalized standard deviation of log-determinants across subsamples
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviation across the 15 subsamples is the reported variation.
rows.note: The paper describes the shaded standard-deviation band as barely visible. This concerns NTK log-determinants under subsampling.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Fitted FLODANCE on each subsample and extrapolated log-determinants to n = 10,000.
rows.measure: Relative error of predicted mean log-determinant
rows.uncertainty: Variation across the ensemble is shown as a shaded region; no numerical uncertainty value stated.
rows.note: This evaluates predictions of NTK log-determinants, not language-model loss.

rows.subject: Multi-output Gaussian process with a Matérn kernel
rows.operation_detail: Measured ratios of successive covariance-matrix determinants as the number of spatial points increases.
rows.note: The paper describes the empirical ratios as exhibiting a smooth trend consistent with the theoretical behavior. This is a kernel determinant result, not a pretraining-loss result.

rows.subject: Multi-output Gaussian process with a Matérn kernel
rows.operation_detail: Fitted FLODANCE on a small interval and extrapolated the covariance-matrix log-determinant.
rows.note: This evaluates covariance-matrix log-determinant extrapolation in a Matérn-kernel setting, not language-model loss.
